study type: Longitudinal cohort study with repeated cross-sectional surveys
exposure: inability to receive scheduled medical examinations
cohort: Expectant and nursing mothers (approximately 15,000 individuals annually) in Fukushima, Japan, affected by the nuclear accident.
finding: The prevalence of depressive symptoms among mothers was highest immediately after childbirth and decreased over time, with the nuclear accident having a prolonged impact, especially on those who gave birth immediately after the disaster.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was identified as a characteristic among mothers who received telephone parenting counseling.
followup_time: Up to 4 years after childbirth for individual follow-ups, with survey data collected annually over 8 years (FY 2011-2018).
